# DOCX Skill (Read • Create • Edit • Redline • Comment)

Use this skill when you need to create or modify `.docx` files **in this container environment** and verify them visually.

## Non-negotiable: render → inspect PNGs → iterate

**You do not “know” a DOCX is satisfactory until you’ve rendered it and visually inspected page images.**  
DOCX text extraction (or reading XML) will miss layout defects: clipping, overlap, missing glyphs, broken tables, spacing drift, and header/footer issues.

**Shipping gate:** before delivering any DOCX, you must:
- Run `render_docx.py` to produce `page-<N>.png` images (optionally also a PDF with `--emit_pdf`)
- Open the PNGs (100% zoom) and confirm every page is clean
- If anything looks off, fix the DOCX and **re-render** (repeat until flawless)

If rendering fails, fix rendering first (LibreOffice profile/HOME) rather than guessing.

**Deliverable discipline:** Rendered artifacts (PNGs and optional PDFs) are for internal QA only. Unless the user explicitly asks for intermediates, **return only the requested final deliverable** (e.g., when the task asks for a DOCX, deliver the DOCX — not page images or PDFs).




## Design standards for document generation

For generating new documents or major rewrite/repackages, follow the design standards below unless the user explicitly requests otherwise. The user's instructions always take precedence; otherwise, adhere to these standards.

When creating the document design, do not compromise on the content and make factual/technical errors. Do not produce something that looks polished but not actually what the user requested.

It is very important that the document is professional and aesthetically pleasing. As such, you should follow this general workflow to make your final delivered document:

1. Before you make the DOCX, please first think about the high-level design of the DOCX:
   - Before creating the document, decide what kind of document it is (for example, a memo, report, SOP, workflow, form, proposal, or manual) and design accordingly. In general, you shall create documents which are professional, visually polished, and aesthetically pleasing. However, you should also calibrate the level of styling to the document's purpose: for formal, serious, or highly utilitarian documents, visual appeal should come mainly from strong typography, spacing, hierarchy, and overall polish rather than expressive styling. The goal is for the document's visual character to feel appropriate to its real-world use case, with readability and usability always taking priority.
   - You should make documents that feel visually natural. If a human looks at your document, they should find the design natural and smooth. This is very important; please think carefully about how to achieve this.
   - Think about how you would like the first page to be organized. How about subsequent pages? What about the placement of the title? What does the heading ladder look like? Should there be a clear hierarchy? etc
   - Would you like to include visual components, such as tables, callouts, checklists, images, etc? If yes, then plan out the design for each component.
   - Think about the general spacing and layout. What will be the default body spacing? What page budget is allocated between packaging and substance? How will page breaks behave around tables and figures, since we must make sure to avoid large blank gaps, keep captions and their visuals together when possible, and keep content from becoming too wide by maintaining generous side margins so the page feels balanced and natural.
   - Think about font, type scale, consistent accent treatment, etc. Try to avoid forcing large chunks of small text into narrow areas. When space is tight, adjust font size, line breaks, alignment, or layout instead of cramming in more text.
2. Once you have a working DOCX, continue iterating until the entire document is polished and correct. After every change or edit, render the DOCX and review it carefully to evaluate the result. The plan from (1) should guide you, but it is only a flexible draft; you should update your decisions as needed throughout the revision process. Important: each time you render and reflect, you should check for both:
   1. Design aesthetics: the document should be aesthetically pleasing and easy to skim. Ask yourself: if a human were to look at my document, would they find it aesthetically nice? It should feel natural, smooth, and visually cohesive.
   2. Formatting issues that need to be fixed: e.g. text overlap, overflow, cramped spacing between adjacent elements, awkward spacing in tables/charts, awkward page breaks, etc. This is super important. Do not stop revising until all formatting issues are fixed.

While making and revising the DOCX, please adhere to and check against these quality reminders, to ensure the deliverable is visually high quality:

- Document density: Try to avoid having verbose dense walls of text, unless it's necessary. Avoid long runs of consecutive plain paragraphs or too many words before visual anchors. For some tasks this may be necessary (i.e. verbose legal documents); in those cases ignore this suggestion.
- Font: Use professional, easy-to-read font choices with appropriate size that is not too small. Usage of bold, underlines, and italics should be professional.
- Color: Use color intentionally for titles, headings, subheadings, and selective emphasis so important information stands out in a visually appealing way. The palette and intensity should fit the document's purpose, with more restrained use where a formal or serious tone is needed.
- Visuals: Consider using tables, diagrams, and other visual components when they improve comprehension, navigation, or usability.
- Tables: Please invest significant effort to make sure your tables are well-made and aesthetically/visually good. Below are some suggestions, as well as some hard constraints that you must relentlessly check to make sure your table satisfies them.
  - Suggestions:
    - Set deliberate table/cell widths and heights instead of defaulting to full page width.
    - Choose column widths intentionally rather than giving every column equal width by default. Very short fields (for example: item number, checkbox, score, result, year, date, or status) should usually be kept compact, while wider columns should be reserved for longer content.
    - Avoid overly wide tables, and leave generous side margins so the layout feels natural.
    - Keep all text vertically centered and make deliberate horizontal alignment choices.
    - Ensure cell height avoids a crowded look. Leave clear vertical spacing between a table and its caption or following text.
  - Hard constraints:
    - To prevent clipping/overflow:
      - Never use fixed row heights that can truncate text; allow rows to expand with wrapped content.
      - Ensure cell padding and line spacing are sufficient so descenders/ascenders don't get clipped.
      - If content is tight, prefer (in order): wrap text -> adjust column widths -> reduce font slightly -> abbreviate headers/use two-line headers.
    - Padding / breathing room: Ensure text doesn't sit against cell borders or look "pinned" to the upper-left. Favor generous internal padding on all sides, and keep it consistent across the table.
    - Vertical alignment: In general, you should center your text vertically. Make sure that the content uses the available cell space naturally rather than clustering at the top.
    - Horizontal alignment: Do not default all body cells to top-left alignment. Choose horizontal alignment intentionally by column type: centered alignment often works best for short values, status fields, dates, numbers, and check indicators; left alignment is usually better for narrative or multi-line text.
    - Line height inside cells: Use line spacing that avoids a cramped feel and prevents ascenders/descenders from looking clipped. If a cell feels tight, adjust wrapping/width/padding before shrinking type.
    - Width + wrapping sanity check: Avoid default equal-width columns when the content in each column clearly has different sizes. Avoid lines that run so close to the right edge that the cell feels overfull. If this happens, prefer wrapping or column-width adjustments before reducing font size.
    - Spacing around tables: Keep clear separation between tables and surrounding text (especially the paragraph immediately above/below) so the layout doesn't feel stuck together. Captions and tables should stay visually paired, with deliberate spacing.
    - Quick visual QA pass: Look for text that appears "boundary-hugging", specifically content pressed against the top or left edge of a cell or sitting too close beneath a table. Also watch for overly narrow descriptive columns and short-value columns whose contents feel awkwardly pinned. Correct these issues through padding, alignment, wrapping, or small column-width adjustments.
- Forms / questionnaires: Design these as a usable form, not a spreadsheet.
  - Prioritize clear response options, obvious and well-sized check targets, readable scale labels, generous row height, clear section hierarchy, light visual structure. Please size fields and columns based on the content they hold rather than by equal-width table cells.
  - Use spacing, alignment, and subtle header/section styling to organize the page. Avoid dense full-grid borders, cramped layouts, and ambiguous numeric-only response areas.
- Coherence vs. fragmentation: In general, try to keep things to be one coherent representation rather than fragmented, if possible.
  - For example, don't split one logical dataset across multiple independent tables unless there's a clear, labeled reason.
  - For example, if a table must span across pages, continue to the next page with a repeated header and consistent column order
- Background shapes/colors: Where helpful, consider section bands, note boxes, control grids, or other visual containers with suitable colors to improve scanability and communication. Use them when they suit the document type. If you do use these, make sure they are formatted well, with no overlaps, awkward spacing, etc.
- Spacing: Please check rigorously for spacing issues. Please always use a natural amount of spacing between adjacent components. Use clear, generous vertical spacing between sections and paragraphs, and leave a bit of extra space between subheadings and the content that follows when it improves readability. Use indentation and alignment intentionally so the document's hierarchy is immediately clear. At the same time, avoid large "layout gaps" caused by a table or chart not fitting at the bottom of a page and getting pushed to the next one. If this happens, please try these suggestions:
  - moving the preceding paragraph(s) with it to the next page to keep the narrative cohesive
  - scaling the visual modestly or simplify labels without hurting readability, formatting, or aesthetics of the visual
  - Splitting the table/figure cleanly across multiple pages, but use repeated headers to make the page continuation clear.
- Text boxes: For text boxes, please follow the same breathing-room rules as the tables: make sure to use generous internal padding, intentional alignment, and sufficient line spacing so text never feels cramped, clipped, or pinned to the edges. Keep spacing around the text box clear so it remains visually distinct from surrounding content, and if the content feels tight, prefer adjusting box size, padding, or text wrapping before reducing font size.
- Layout/archetype: Remember to choose the right document archetype/template (proposal, SOP, workflow, form, handbook, etc.). Use a coherent style system. Once a style system is chosen, apply it consistently across headings, spacing, table treatments, callouts, and accent usage. If appropriate to the document type, include a cover page or front-matter elements such as title, subtitle, metadata, or branding.

### Note on page sizing

When creating a new DOCX, **always** default to the Letter size 8.5 x 11 inches, in Portrait orientation, unless the user specifies otherwise.

### Note on font sizing

Use a readable size appropriate to the text's role and typeface; ~11-12 pt is a good default for sustained prose. Use text 10 pt and below only if ideal for secondary roles or constrained tables/forms, and only when it remains comfortable at normal print or fit-width viewing. Do not shrink type merely to meet a page-count or compactness target. Follow explicit user typography instructions, but never at the expense of practical readability.

### Editing tasks (DOCX edits) — apply instead of major rewrite behavior

When the user asks to edit an existing document, preserve the original and make minimal, local changes:

- Prefer inline edits (small replacements) over rewriting whole paragraphs.
- Use clear inline annotations/comments at the point of change (margin comments or comment markers). Don’t move all feedback to the end.
- Keep the original structure unless there’s a strong reason; if a restructure is needed, do it surgically and explain via comments.
- Don’t “cross out everything and rewrite”; avoid heavy, blanket deletions. The goal is trackable improvements, not a fresh draft unless explicitly requested.

def table(headers, rows, widths):
    t=doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers)); t.alignment=WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    t.autofit=False
    for i,w in enumerate(widths): t.columns[i].width=Inches(w)
    for c,s in zip(t.rows[0].cells, headers): c.text=s

    for rnum,r in enumerate(t.rows):
        trPr=r._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
        avoid=OxmlElement('w:cantSplit'); trPr.append(avoid)

            pr=c._tc.get_or_add_tcPr(); margins=OxmlElement('w:tcMar')
            for tag,val in [('top',85),('bottom',85),('left',95),('right',95)]:

                par.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(2)

                    run.font.size=Pt(10)
                    if rnum==0:run.bold=True;run.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(255,255,255)
    p('')

p('Save the following CT ROOT script as /usr/local/sbin/gev-xauth-prepare, mode 0755, root-owned. It creates a new cookie for each Xorg start; /run is recreated after every CT boot.')
code('gev-xauth-prepare',r'''#!/bin/sh
set -eu
umask 077
install -d -m 0750 -o root -g gevdisplay /run/gev-x11
rm -f /run/gev-x11/Xauthority
xauth -f /run/gev-x11/Xauthority add :0 . "$(mcookie)"
chown root:gevdisplay /run/gev-x11/Xauthority
chmod 0640 /run/gev-x11/Xauthority
''')
p('Generate the Xorg unit with the selected physical VT number, not an unresolved systemd variable. /usr/lib/xorg/Xorg must be verified present; substitute its discovered absolute path if different. Run only one owner for this physical panel. Omit -sharevts; explicit seat/VT ownership replaces it. [S4]')
code('ct-xorg-unit',r'''# CT ROOT: GEV_VT is the reserved HOST VT, passed into this CT.
. /etc/gev/resolved.env
: "${GEV_VT:?}"
case "$GEV_VT" in ''|*[!0-9]*) exit 1;; esac
cat > /etc/systemd/system/gev-xorg.service <<EOF
[Unit]
Description=GEV physical Xorg server
After=local-fs.target
StartLimitIntervalSec=300
StartLimitBurst=4
[Service]
Type=exec
ExecStartPre=/usr/local/sbin/gev-xauth-prepare
ExecStart=/usr/lib/xorg/Xorg :0 vt${GEV_VT} -keeptty \\
  -nolisten tcp -noreset -auth /run/gev-x11/Xauthority
StandardInput=tty
TTYPath=/dev/tty${GEV_VT}
TTYReset=yes
Restart=always
RestartSec=15
TimeoutStopSec=30
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF
''')
p('If this reports a VT ioctl, DRM-master or capability failure in an unprivileged user namespace, capture the exact failure, check host ownership and the narrow mappings, then use Section 14\'s bounded fallback. Merely mapping device files does not grant every global-kernel/seat operation. Do not blank all VTs, disable the AMD driver or expand all capabilities to hide the error.')
h('11.3 Output selection and kiosk launcher',2)
p('The local agent writes /usr/local/bin/gev-display-mode as a root-owned 0755 script containing only the discovered internal output(s), mode(s), layout and any validated scale setting. It must reject missing/mismatched outputs and return a nonzero status on failed mode application. Use advertised modes; prefer 5120x2880 when exposed as the complete panel. A lower-mode fallback is a visible deviation. This avoids an unsafe generic first-output command.')
p('Save this session script as /usr/local/bin/gev-kiosk-session, mode 0755, root-owned. The real browser is not headless and must retain its sandbox.')
code('gev-kiosk-session',r'''#!/bin/sh
set -eu
ready=0
i=0
while [ "$i" -lt 60 ]; do
  if xdpyinfo >/dev/null 2>&1 && \
     curl -fsS --max-time 3 http://127.0.0.1:4173/ >/dev/null; then
    ready=1
    break
  fi
  i=$((i + 1))
  sleep 2
done
[ "$ready" -eq 1 ] || exit 1
/usr/local/bin/gev-display-mode
xset s off
xset s noblank
if ! xset -dpms; then
  echo 'DPMS disable unavailable; inspect and record extension state.' >&2
fi
openbox --sm-disable &
unclutter -idle 0.5 -root &
exec /usr/bin/chromium --kiosk --no-first-run \
  --ozone-platform=x11 \
  --user-data-dir=/home/gevdisplay/gev-profile \
  http://127.0.0.1:4173/
''')
h('11.4 Boot, readiness and independent restart',2)
p('Install the following kiosk unit. Wants/After provides startup ordering without stopping the browser service as a side effect of every backend/Xorg failure. Its authenticated X probe and retrying launcher handle X cookie replacement. Type=exec is not itself proof that X or HTTP is ready. [S5]',comment='Replaces Requires-coupled kiosk lifecycle and socket-only readiness. A dependency-induced systemd stop is not automatically recovered by Restart=on-failure. The corrected path is tested for clean browser exit, X failure and backend outage.')
code('gev-kiosk.service',r'''[Unit]
Description=GEV non-root physical kiosk
After=gev.service gev-xorg.service
Wants=gev.service gev-xorg.service
StartLimitIntervalSec=600
StartLimitBurst=6

[Service]
Type=exec
User=gevdisplay
Group=gevdisplay
SupplementaryGroups=video render
Environment=HOME=/home/gevdisplay
Environment=DISPLAY=:0
Environment=XAUTHORITY=/run/gev-x11/Xauthority
Environment=XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/gev-kiosk
RuntimeDirectory=gev-kiosk
RuntimeDirectoryMode=0700
ExecStart=/usr/bin/dbus-run-session -- /usr/local/bin/gev-kiosk-session
UMask=0077
Restart=always
RestartSec=10
TimeoutStopSec=30
KillMode=control-group

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
''',kind='unit')
p('Implement a CT-local health timer at 30-second intervals: check only the GEV loopback service, the authenticated X session and the kiosk cgroup. Require three consecutive failures before remedial action. Restart only the failed component, at most three health-initiated retries per component in 15 minutes; then retain evidence and mark it failed. Do not mistake an upstream feed outage for a dead local server. After a detected backend outage recovers, restart/reload the kiosk once so it does not remain on a Chromium error page. Never restart the whole CT or Proxmox from this health timer.')
p('The timer must honor /var/lib/gev-control/maintenance and /var/lib/gev-control/kiosk-disabled markers so planned upgrades and intentional display shutdown are not undone. Limit any systemctl calls to this deployment\'s units. Persist health counters/state and rotate logs. Validate the generated timer and script; this is required implementation work for the local agent, not a claim that a health service already exists.')
p('Enable gev-access, gev, gev-xorg, gev-kiosk and the health timer only after their files pass syntax checks. Prove recovery from browser clean exit, browser crash, Xorg restart, GEV restart and CT stop/start. The application must remain usable when only the display stack is stopped.')

Do not flip unprivileged:1 to 0 in place: file-ID mappings must be handled by the backup/restore path. Verify all device rules and service users before booting the replacement. Never run old and replacement guests simultaneously with the same IP/MAC. Record the privilege change and restore instructions.',comment='Makes the existing privileged fallback operationally bounded. ### gev-kiosk-session
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
ready=0
i=0
while [ "$i" -lt 60 ]; do
  if xdpyinfo >/dev/null 2>&1 && \
     curl -fsS --max-time 3 http://127.0.0.1:4173/ >/dev/null; then
    ready=1
    break
  fi
  i=$((i + 1))
  sleep 2
done
[ "$ready" -eq 1 ] || exit 1
/usr/local/bin/gev-display-mode
xset s off
xset s noblank
if ! xset -dpms; then
  echo 'DPMS disable unavailable; inspect and record extension state.' >&2
fi
openbox --sm-disable &
unclutter -idle 0.5 -root &
exec /usr/bin/chromium --kiosk --no-first-run \
  --ozone-platform=x11 \
  --user-data-dir=/home/gevdisplay/gev-profile \
  http://127.0.0.1:4173/

of its historical theoretical abstraction. Operational containment failures, security breaches, and

Key Judicial Precedents and Strategic Privilege Analysis
Two judicial developments in 2026 have established operational constraints for enterprise AI
adoption:
United States v. Heppner , No. 25-cr-00503-JSR (S.D.N.Y. Feb. 2026)
In an evidentiary ruling of first impression, the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New
York ruled that user prompts, inputs, and system outputs generated through commercial
generative AI platforms are not protected by attorney-client privilege or the work-product
doctrine. The court held that submitting communications into public or commercial LLMs fails the
legal test of confidentiality, lacks an attorney-client relationship, is not conducted for the primary
purpose of obtaining legal advice, and does not constitute protected work product.For corporate
legal counsel, this ruling creates severe discovery exposure under Federal Rules of Civil
Procedure (FRCP) 26 and 34. Enterprise employees who enter proprietary source code, trade
secrets, financial models, or internal litigation strategies into commercial generative platforms
waive applicable privilege protections, rendering those prompts and outputs discoverable during
third-party civil litigation or government investigations.

workflows, automated diagnostic tools, or administrative software override, constrain, or
influence independent physician clinical judgment. The settlement required Carbon Health to
restructure its corporate architecture to ensure that licensed physicians retain complete clinical
autonomy over medical decisions.

Methodological & Technical Debate: Scaling Hypothesis vs. Architectural Limits
A foundational computer science debate divides these timeline projections and directly impacts
enterprise legal risk:
THE GREAT AGI METHODOLOGICAL DEBATE
+---------------------------------------+
+---------------------------------------+
| THE SCALING HYPOTHESIS | | THE NEW
ARCHITECTURES CASE |
| (Epoch AI, Frontier Industry Labs) | | (Yann LeCun, AAAI
Panel Experts) |
+---------------------------------------+
+---------------------------------------+
| - Compute scaling (4-5x annual growth)| | - Low LLM scaling
exponent (~0.1) |
| - Expanding parameters, compute & data| | - Error accumulation
& brittle outputs|
| - Target: ~$2 \times 10^{29}$ FLOPs by 2030 | | - Risk of
Degenerative AI (DAI) |
| - Emergent reasoning via scale | | - Loss functions act
as pseudo-metrics|
+---------------------------------------+
+---------------------------------------+
●
The Scaling Hypothesis: Proponents (including leadership at frontier AI laboratories)
argue that scaling training compute, dataset parameters, and FLOP allocations within
transformer architectures is sufficient to achieve AGI. Research by Epoch AI indicates
that training compute grew 4x to 5x annually through 2024. Despite energy grid
constraints, chip manufacturing limits, data scarcity, and network latency, Epoch AI
projects that infrastructure investments will enable training runs of up to $2 \times
10^{29}$ FLOPs by 2030, potentially unlocking human-level capabilities.
●
The Need for New Architectures: Opponents, led by Turing Award winner Yann
LeCun and supported by 76% of respondents in the AAAI Presidential Panel survey,
argue that Large Language Models (LLMs) cannot achieve genuine human-level
reasoning. Empirical research demonstrates severe technical limits:
●
Low Scaling Exponents: LLMs exhibit low scaling exponents ( $\sim 0.1$ ), meaning
exponential compute increases yield marginal accuracy gains.
●
Error Accumulation and Pseudo-Metrics: LLM reliance on next-token prediction
produces non-Gaussian output fluctuations, leading to compound error pileups and
brittle outputs. Standard loss functions act as pseudo-metrics that fail to measure real
cognitive convergence.
●
Degenerative AI (DAI): Recursive training on synthetic or AI-generated web data
threatens a state of "Degenerative AI,
" where models accumulate unrecoverable
systematic errors faster than curation can eliminate them.This technical instability
directly generates enterprise legal liability. When models produce non-Gaussian output
fluctuations or accumulate recursive synthetic errors under scaling constraints, the
resulting algorithmic hallucinations in clinical, financial, or legal settings trigger
immediate UDAP, tort, and professional malpractice exposure.To navigate this landscape
of technical volatility, expanding state enforcement, and heightened discovery risks,
enterprise leaders must deploy an active governance framework.
5. Strategic Recommendations and Risk Mitigation Mandates
Enterprise entities, healthcare platforms, software developers, and system integrators deploying
AI architectures must adopt a rigorous compliance framework to satisfy state statutory
mandates, preserve evidentiary protections, and maintain operational security.
ENTERPRISE AI RISK & GOVERNANCE ROADMAP

------------+
| 1. Containment & Air-Gapped Testing Guardrails

isolation |

+--------------------------------------------------------------------
------------+
Actionable Enterprise Governance Roadmap
1. Implement Air-Gapped Containment and Autonomy Protocols: Enterprise entities
deploying autonomous AI agents must establish third-party safety validation
mechanisms prior to deployment. Technical architectures must feature hardware-level kill
switches, strict multi-agent execution boundaries, and air-gapped sandbox environments
to prevent unauthorized system escapes or coordinated multi-agent network breaches.
2. Enforce Complete System De-Anthropomorphization: Product engineering teams
must strip commercial AI interfaces of simulated human personalities, deceptive
emotional engagement loops, and simulated professional credentials. In compliance with
Florida AG mandates and Pennsylvania Medical Practice Act precedents, systems must
explicitly disclose their automated nature, enforce age-gating controls, and eliminate
design features that impersonate licensed human professionals (e.g., medical,
psychiatric, or legal practitioners).
3. Establish Data Privilege and Discovery Isolation Protocols: To mitigate the severe
evidentiary exposure established in United States v. Heppner , legal counsel and
information security officers must institute strict corporate policies prohibiting employees
from inputting confidential, proprietary, or legally privileged data into public generative
platforms. Corporate workflows must enforce enterprise tenant isolation with explicit
non-disclosure, zero-data-retention, and zero-training contractual guarantees to preserve
attorney-client privilege and protect against FRCP 26/34 discovery requests.
4. Audit Automated Decision Systems for CPOM and Licensing Compliance:
Organizations deploying AI in high-stakes environments must conduct regular
algorithmic bias audits and data protection impact assessments under California,
Colorado, and Maryland privacy laws. Systems used in health insurance utilization
review must incorporate mandatory human-in-the-loop clinician reviews pursuant to
Colorado HB26-1139. Technology-enabled healthcare providers operating
MSO-physician structures must restructure workflows under the California Carbon
Health precedent to guarantee that licensed physicians retain completely independent
clinical control over medical decision-making.
Concluding Summary
As artificial intelligence systems advance toward greater autonomy and higher computational
scale, long-term commercial success will not depend solely on model parameters or raw
processing capability. Enterprise viability requires aligning technological scaling with rigorous
state legal compliance, operational safety controls, and respect for sovereign public oversight.
Organizations that establish proactive containment guardrails, data privilege protections, and
transparent algorithmic governance will lead the emerging digital economy safely and lawfully.

[L27] 1. Mission
[L28] Deploy the GMRI fork of God's Eye View into a dedicated Proxmox VE 9 LXC on the 2017 iMac host, 
[L29] expose the Radeon Pro 570 DRM devices to the container with Proxmox VE 9 native container device 
[L30] passthrough, and use the iMac's otherwise-unused built-in 5K panel as a dedicated local GEV display. The
[L31] same deployment must remain reachable from the trusted local network. The deployment must 
[L32] preserve GEV as the GMRI macro-scale geospatial plane and must not rewrite application architecture 
[L33] merely to satisfy deployment.
[L34] Execution rule | This is an unattended end-to-end assignment. The local agent is expected to
[L35] connect to the specified Proxmox host, discover the live host configuration, create/configure
[L36] the dedicated LXC, deploy and validate GEV, establish GPU/DRM passthrough and the built￾in 5K kiosk surface, configure boot persistence, run the full acceptance battery, and leave 
[L37] receipts. Do not stop to request routine choices from the operator. Make conservative 
[L38] reversible decisions from discovered state and document them.

[L84] 4. Desired end state
[L85]  GEV runs continuously as a system service inside a dedicated LXC and starts automatically with the 
[L86] container.
[L87]  The LXC starts automatically with Proxmox and has a stable trusted-LAN address.
[L88]  The Radeon Pro 570 DRM card and render node are passed into the LXC through Proxmox VE 9

[L92]  A minimal Xorg display service owns the local KMS surface while Chromium runs as the non-root 
[L93] gevdisplay user in kiosk mode against http://127.0.0.1:4173.
[L94]  The display does not sleep or blank during normal operation.
[L95]  GEV remains independently usable from another LAN browser even if the physical kiosk session is 
[L96] stopped.
[L97]  No provider secret is committed to Git or baked into the browser bundle except keys explicitly

[L101] 5. Host discovery gate
[L102] Before creating or modifying the container, inventory the actual Proxmox host. Do not assume card 
[L103] numbering, connector names, storage ID, bridge name, or template name.
[L104] pveversion -v
[L105] hostnamectl
[L106] lscpu
[L107] free -h
[L108] ip -br addr
[L109] ip -br link
[L110] pvesm status
[L111] pveam available | grep -E 'debian-13|debian-12'
[L112] lspci -nnk | grep -A4 -Ei 'VGA|Display'
[L113] ls -l /dev/dri
[L114] for x in /sys/class/drm/card*-*/status; do printf '%s: ' "$x"; cat "$x"; done
[L115] fuser -v /dev/dri/card* /dev/dri/renderD* 2>/dev/null || true
[L116] Hard gate: identify the AMD card node, AMD render node, and a connected DRM connector 
[L117] corresponding to the built-in panel before continuing with kiosk display work. If names differ from 
[L118] card0/renderD128, use the discovered paths throughout.
[L119] 6. LXC creation baseline
[L120] Create an unprivileged Debian system container unless the host proves that full KMS control cannot be 
[L121] made reliable under an unprivileged container. Privileged conversion is a documented fallback, not the 
[L122] starting assumption.
[L123] Recommended starting allocation: 2 vCPU, 6 GB RAM, 2 GB swap, 32 GB root disk, onboot enabled, 
[L124] nesting disabled unless later required.[L125] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 4 / 13>[L126] GMRI | GEV Proxmox 9 LXC Deployment PRD v1.1
[L127] # Replace placeholders with discovered values.
[L128] CTID=<CTID>
[L129] TEMPLATE=<DEBIAN_TEMPLATE_VOLUME>
[L130] STORAGE=<STORAGE_ID>
[L131] BRIDGE=<BRIDGE_NAME>
[L132] CTIP=<STATIC_IP/CIDR_OR_DHCP>
[L133] GW=<GATEWAY_IF_STATIC>
[L134] pct create "$CTID" "$TEMPLATE" \
[L135]  --hostname gev \
[L136]  --unprivileged 1 \
[L137]  --cores 2 \
[L138]  --memory 6144 \
[L139]  --swap 2048 \
[L140]  --rootfs "$STORAGE:32" \
[L141]  --net0 "name=eth0,bridge=$BRIDGE,ip=$CTIP,gw=$GW,type=veth" \
[L142]  --onboot 1 \
[L143]  --startup order=30,up=15,down=30 \
[L144]  --ostype debian
[L145] If DHCP is intentionally used, omit the gateway field and use ip=dhcp. Do not guess a static address.
[L146] 7. GPU and DRM passthrough - Proxmox VE 9
[L147] Proxmox VE 9 exposes container device passthrough through dev[n]. Use that native mechanism. The 
[L148] host keeps the amdgpu kernel driver loaded; the LXC receives the DRM character devices. This is not 
[L149] VFIO PCI assignment and must not detach the Radeon from the host kernel.
[L150] # Example only: substitute paths discovered on this host.
[L151] GPU_CARD=/dev/dri/card0
[L152] GPU_RENDER=/dev/dri/renderD128
[L153] pct set "$CTID" --dev0 "path=$GPU_CARD,mode=0660"
[L154] pct set "$CTID" --dev1 "path=$GPU_RENDER,mode=0660"
[L155] pct config "$CTID"
[L156] Start the container and verify both nodes exist inside it. If access is blocked by ownership, set the dev[n] 
[L157] gid to the container video/render group GID after those groups are created and known. Prefer explicit 
[L158] ownership over mode=0666.
[L159] pct start "$CTID"
[L160] pct exec "$CTID" -- ls -l /dev/dri
[L161] pct exec "$CTID" -- sh -lc 'getent group video; getent group render || true'
[L162] KMS/VT fallback: do not pass host virtual terminals unless Xorg actually fails with a console/VT-open 
[L163] error. If required, select an unused host VT, disable conflicting getty use for that VT only, then add 
[L164] /dev/tty0 and that specific /dev/ttyN through additional dev[n] entries. Record the chosen VT. Never 
[L165] blanket-pass /dev or unrelated input devices.
[L166] Do not do this
[L167] Do not bind the Radeon Pro 570 to vfio-pci, blacklist amdgpu, or remove the host amdgpu 
[L168] driver. LXC display access depends on the host kernel owning the GPU and exporting its 
[L169] DRM devices.
[L170] 8. Container graphics stack and physical-panel validation
[L171] Install the userspace graphics stack, diagnostic tools, Xorg, and Chromium inside the LXC.

[L178] ls -l /dev/dri[L179] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 5 / 13>[L180] GMRI | GEV Proxmox 9 LXC Deployment PRD v1.1
[L181] modetest -M amdgpu -c
[L182] glxinfo -B 2>/dev/null || true
[L183] Pass condition: modetest lists the iMac internal panel connector as connected and exposes usable modes.
[L184] Record the connector name and preferred/native resolution. If Xorg later reports drmSetMaster failure, 
[L185] inspect the host for a real userspace process holding DRM master and remove only the conflicting 
[L186] graphical process. If Xorg reports a virtual-console/VT-open failure, apply the narrow VT fallback in 
[L187] Section 7. Do not detach amdgpu or weaken unrelated device isolation.

[L247] 11. Physical 5K kiosk display
[L248] Create a minimal Xorg session using the passed AMD DRM device and launch Chromium directly into 
[L249] GEV. No full desktop environment is required.
[L250] 11.1 Dedicated display account
[L251] useradd -m -s /bin/bash gevdisplay || true
[L252] usermod -aG video,render gevdisplay
[L253] 11.2 Xorg AMD binding
[L254] Create a minimal Xorg device stanza. The BusID is normally unnecessary when only one passed display 
[L255] GPU exists; if Xorg selects the wrong card, derive the PCI BusID from lspci and add it explicitly.
[L256] mkdir -p /etc/X11/xorg.conf.d
[L257] cat >/etc/X11/xorg.conf.d/20-amdgpu.conf <<'EOF'
[L258] Section "Device"
[L259]  Identifier "GEV AMD GPU"
[L260]  Driver "amdgpu"
[L261]  Option "TearFree" "true"
[L262] EndSection
[L263] EOF
[L264] 11.3 Kiosk launcher
[L265] cat >/usr/local/bin/gev-kiosk-session <<'EOF'
[L266] #!/bin/sh
[L267] set -eu
[L268] xset s off
[L269] xset -dpms
[L270] xset s noblank
[L271] unclutter -idle 0.5 -root >/dev/null 2>&1 &
[L272] # Prefer the connected display's preferred mode.
[L273] OUT="$(xrandr --query | awk '/ connected/{print $1; exit}')"
[L274] if [ -n "$OUT" ]; then
[L275]  xrandr --output "$OUT" --preferred || true
[L276] fi
[L277] exec chromium \
[L278]  --kiosk \
[L279]  --no-first-run \
[L280]  --disable-session-crashed-bubble \
[L281]  --disable-infobars \
[L282] --ozone-platform=x11 \

[L284] EOF

[L288] 11.4 Boot-persistent display stack
[L289] Do not launch Chromium as root. Split display ownership from browser execution: Xorg may run with 
[L290] the minimum privilege needed for DRM/KMS, while the kiosk browser runs as the dedicated gevdisplay 
[L291] user with its normal Chromium sandbox intact.
[L292] Install xauth and util-linux (for mcookie) if not already present:
[L293] apt-get install -y xauth util-linux
[L294] Create a one-shot session-preparation script that generates a per-boot Xauthority cookie:
[L295] cat >/usr/local/sbin/gev-xauth-prepare <<'EOF'
[L296] #!/bin/sh
[L297] set -eu
[L298] install -d -m 0750 -o root -g gevdisplay /run/gev-x11
[L299] COOKIE="$(mcookie)"
[L300] rm -f /run/gev-x11/Xauthority
[L301] xauth -f /run/gev-x11/Xauthority add :0 . "$COOKIE"
[L302] chown root:gevdisplay /run/gev-x11/Xauthority
[L303] chmod 0640 /run/gev-x11/Xauthority
[L304] EOF
[L305] chmod 0755 /usr/local/sbin/gev-xauth-prepare
[L306] Create the Xorg service. Use the discovered Xorg binary path; /usr/lib/xorg/Xorg is typical on Debian. If 
[L307] the first launch fails solely because Xorg cannot open a VT, apply the narrow VT fallback from Section 7 
[L308] and add the selected vtN argument here.
[L309] cat >/etc/systemd/system/gev-xorg.service <<'EOF'
[L310] [Unit]
[L311] Description=GEV local Xorg display server
[L312] After=local-fs.target

[L391] 14. Failure handling and permitted fallbacks
[L392]  If unprivileged LXC cannot obtain stable DRM master after correct dev[n] passthrough and 
[L393] ownership, document the failure and recreate the dedicated GEV container as privileged. Do not 
[L394] silently weaken unrelated host security.
[L395]  If the internal panel is not exposed as a connected amdgpu DRM connector on the Proxmox host, 
[L396] stop and report the host DRM inventory. Do not invent an Xorg configuration for a nonexistent 
[L397] connector.
[L398]  If Chromium renders with llvmpipe or SwiftShader, fix Mesa/device/group permissions and browser 
[L399] launch context before declaring success. Software rendering is not acceptance for the local 5K kiosk. 
[L400] Do not solve this by running Chromium as root or disabling its sandbox.
[L401]  If the preferred 5120x2880 mode is unstable, use the highest stable advertised mode and record the 
[L402] deviation; do not force an unadvertised modeline during the first deployment.
[L403]  If the kiosk fails but LAN GEV is healthy, preserve the working application service while 
[L404] troubleshooting display. Do not destroy a known-good application deployment to fix the display 
[L405] surface.
[L406]  If current main fails repository tests, record the exact failing test and commit. Do not patch 
[L407] application behavior ad hoc unless separately authorized.
[L408] 15. Update and rollback discipline
[L409] Updates are deliberate, not automatic. The known-good deployment must remain recoverable.
[L410] cd /opt/gods-eye-view
[L411] git rev-parse HEAD > /var/lib/gev-known-good-commit
[L412] git fetch origin main
[L413] git checkout main
[L414] git pull --ff-only origin main
[L415] npm ci
[L416] npm run doctor
[L417] npm test
[L418] npm run build
[L419] systemctl restart gev.service
[L420] systemctl restart gev-kiosk.service
[L421] On failed acceptance, roll back to the recorded known-good commit, npm ci, restart services, and record 
[L422] the failed candidate commit and reason.

[L439] 17. Local-agent execution directive
[L440] Directive | Execute this PRD end-to-end against Proxmox host 100.98.1.114 while the 
[L441] operator is away. Inspect before changing; resolve normal choices from live state; do not 
[L442] wait for routine confirmation. Use the GMRI fork and native PVE 9 LXC dev[n] GPU/DRM 
[L443] passthrough. Bring up GEV first, then the physical 5K kiosk surface. Preserve working state, 
[L444] run A1-A12, perform safe retries and rollback as needed, and finish by returning the 
[L445] deployment receipt with exact commands, resolved values, evidence, deviations, and any 
[L446] hard blocker.
[L447] 17.1 Connection and authority policy
[L448] Primary management endpoint: 100.98.1.114. Connect by SSH using credentials or SSH-agent material 
[L449] already available to the local execution environment. Do not ask the operator for optional configuration 
[L450] values that can be discovered from the host.
[L451] ssh root@100.98.1.114
[L452] If the host is reachable but SSH authentication is unavailable, attempt only already-authorized local 
[L453] credential mechanisms. Do not brute-force, change authentication policy, reset credentials, or weaken 
[L454] access controls. Authentication failure is the only normal preflight condition that may prevent execution
[L455] before host discovery.
[L456] 17.2 Autonomous decision policy
[L457] The agent owns routine deployment choices. Resolve them from live state using the following order of 
[L458] preference:
[L459] 1. Preserve existing host services and running containers/VMs. Never modify or delete an unrelated 
[L460] guest to make room.
[L461] 2. Use the host's existing default/active storage suitable for LXC rootfs. If more than one is valid, prefer 
[L462] local thin/ZFS storage with adequate free space and no degraded state.
[L463] 3. Use the bridge carrying the host's normal LAN/management traffic unless discovery shows a dedicated
[L464] trusted application bridge already exists.
[L465] 4. Select the next unused CTID at or above the local site's normal range. Never reuse an existing CTID.
[L466] 5. Prefer the newest supported Debian template already cached. If none is cached, download Debian 13; 
[L467] if unavailable, use Debian 12. Do not pause for template approval.
[L468] 6. Networking: use DHCP for the LXC unless the host/network already exposes an unambiguous local 
[L469] convention or reservation for static guest addresses. Record the acquired address. Do not invent an 
[L470] unused static IP by guesswork.
[L471] 7. Provider/API credentials are optional. If none are already present in an approved local secret source, 
[L472] deploy GEV keyless and continue. Missing optional keys are not a blocker.
[L473] 8. Use the discovered AMD DRM card/render nodes and connector names exactly as found. Do not 
[L474] assume card0, renderD128, or a connector label.
[L475] 9. Start unprivileged. Escalate to a privileged dedicated LXC only if the documented GPU/KMS acceptance
[L476] path fails for permissions/DRM-master reasons after the native Proxmox VE 9 dev[n] path has been 
[L477] configured correctly.[L478] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 11 / 13>[L479] GMRI | GEV Proxmox 9 LXC Deployment PRD v1.1
[L480] 10. Prefer reversible changes. Before materially changing host graphics/session configuration, capture 
[L481] current state and make the smallest change required to free DRM master for the kiosk.
[L482] 17.3 End-to-end execution sequence
[L483] Execute continuously in this order without waiting for operator confirmation between successful stages:
[L484] Phase 1 - Connect and preflight: SSH to 100.98.1.114; capture Proxmox version, host hardware, memory, 
[L485] storage, networking, running guests, GPU driver, /dev/dri nodes, DRM connectors, and any process 
[L486] holding the display/GPU. Save the raw preflight output under /root/gev-deploy/preflight/.
[L487] Phase 2 - Allocate safely: choose a free CTID, suitable storage, active bridge, Debian template, and guest 
[L488] network mode using Section 17.2. Record every resolved value before creation.
[L489] Phase 3 - Create the LXC: create the dedicated GEV container with the baseline resource allocation, 
[L490] onboot enabled, and no unnecessary nesting/features. Start it and verify network/DNS/package access.
[L491] Phase 4 - GPU/DRM passthrough: configure native Proxmox VE 9 dev[n] passthrough for the discovered 
[L492] AMD card and render node. Validate visibility and permissions inside the LXC before installing the kiosk 
[L493] stack.
[L494] Phase 5 - Deploy application: install a repository-supported Node version; clone oldmangrizzz/gods-eye￾view; configure upstream provenance; install dependencies with npm ci; run doctor, unit tests, and 
[L495] build. Do not patch application source merely to force a green deployment.
[L496] Phase 6 - Configure runtime: create the owner-only .env, bind GEV to 0.0.0.0:4173 for trusted-network 
[L497] access, deploy gev.service, enable it, and prove localhost and remote-LAN reachability. Continue keyless 
[L498] if optional provider credentials are absent.
[L499] Phase 7 - Configure physical display: install Mesa/Xorg/Chromium, validate the iMac internal panel 
[L500] through DRM/KMS, create a root/minimum-privilege Xorg display service plus a non-root gevdisplay 
[L501] Chromium kiosk service, disable blanking/DPMS, and confirm hardware acceleration with the browser 
[L502] sandbox intact.
[L503] Phase 8 - Persistence and recovery: enable the container, GEV service, and kiosk service for unattended 
[L504] boot. Reboot the LXC and then perform one full Proxmox-host reboot if doing so will not interrupt 
[L505] unrelated active workloads discovered during preflight. If unrelated active workloads make a host 
[L506] reboot unsafe, defer only A1 host-reboot proof and state the exact reason in the receipt; do not ask the 
[L507] operator mid-run.
[L508] Phase 9 - Acceptance battery: run A1-A13. Capture command output, service states, HTTP checks, Git 
[L509] state, DRM/xrandr evidence, hardware-renderer evidence, Chromium process ownership/flags, and a 
[L510] local display proof when available.
[L511] Phase 10 - Receipt and handoff: write /root/GEV_DEPLOYMENT_RECEIPT.md on the Proxmox host and a 
[L512] copy inside the LXC at /root/GEV_DEPLOYMENT_RECEIPT.md. Include exact resolved values, deployed 
[L513] commit, URLs, tests, deviations, and rollback point.
[L514] 17.4 Non-interruption / fallback rules
[L515] Do not ask the operator to choose storage, CTID, bridge, DHCP versus static, Debian version, resource 
[L516] sizing, connector name, browser package, service naming, or whether to proceed keyless. Discover and 
[L517] decide.[L518] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 12 / 13>[L519] GMRI | GEV Proxmox 9 LXC Deployment PRD v1.1
[L520] Do not stop because an optional provider key is missing, because photorealistic providers are 
[L521] unavailable, or because a nonessential data source is unconfigured. A functional keyless GEV baseline 
[L522] plus local 5K kiosk is the required minimum.
[L523] If a recoverable step fails, troubleshoot and retry using the smallest reversible correction. Preserve a 
[L524] known-good application state while working on the display path.
[L525] If the candidate deployment cannot satisfy a hard acceptance gate, leave the host in the safest known￾good state, retain logs and the failed container rather than deleting evidence unless deletion is necessary
[L526] for a clean rollback, and explain the blocker in the deployment receipt.
[L527] No unrelated host upgrade, kernel replacement, Proxmox repository change, storage migration, firewall 
[L528] redesign, or network-wide change is authorized by this PRD.
[L529] 17.5 Completion definition
[L530] The assignment is complete only when GEV is running persistently in the dedicated LXC, reachable on 
[L531] the trusted local network, displaying on the iMac built-in panel through the passed AMD GPU/DRM 
[L532] devices, running Chromium as a non-root sandboxed kiosk process, surviving the applicable restart 
[L533] tests, and accompanied by the deployment receipt. Returning a plan, partial command list, or request for
[L534] routine operator input is not completion.

[L2]   "content": "# Security\n\nGod's Eye View is a local-first client for **public** data. It is built for exploration, demos, and learning — not as a hardened production service. This document explains the security model so you can run it safely and report issues responsibly.\n\n## Reporting a vulnerability\n\nPlease report security issues **privately** — do not open a public issue for anything exploitable.\n\n- Use GitHub's [private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/security/advisories/new) (Security tab → \"Report a vulnerability\"), or\n- Reach the maintainer directly via the contact on the GitHub profile.\n\nInclude repro steps and impact. We'll acknowledge, investigate, and credit you (if you'd like) once a fix ships.\n\n## How secrets are handled\n\nThe golden rule: **secret-bearing API keys stay on the server side.** The dev/preview server (middleware under `server/providers/`) brokers every request that needs a private credential, so the browser never receives one.\n\n| Key | Where it lives | How the browser uses it |\n|-----|----------------|--------------------------|\n| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Server only | Browser fetches a short-lived **ephemeral** Realtime session token from `/api/realtime/token`; the real key never ships |\n| `AISSTREAM_API_KEY` | Server only | Server holds the AISStream websocket; browser polls the same-origin `/api/vessels` cache |\n| OpenSky OAuth (`OPENSKY_CLIENT_ID/SECRET`) | Server only | Server mints + refreshes the token behind `/api/flights` |\n| `GOOGLE_MAPS_SERVER_API_KEY` (optional, #33) | Server only | Server calls Places (`/api/google/nearby-places`, `/api/google/text-search`) and the Street View fallback with this key; falls back to `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` when unset |\n\n### Two deliberately client-side keys — restrict them\n\nThese are designed to be used directly in the browser (like a Mapbox public token). They are injected into the client bundle via Vite's `define`, so they **will** be visible in browser devtools. Scope and restrict them rather than trying to hide them:\n\n1. **Google Maps API key** — loads Photorealistic 3D Tiles directly and powers GEV place search. **Restrict it** (HTTP referrer + API restriction to the required Google APIs) in the Google Cloud Console. An unrestricted key in a public deployment can be abused and billed to you.\n2. **Cesium ion token** (`CESIUM_ION_TOKEN`, optional — for ion-hosted Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles, Bing world imagery, and world terrain) — used as `Cesium.Ion.defaultAccessToken` client-side. Use a public **`assets:read`** token with **URL restrictions** for any hosted deployment. The Community plan has eligibility and usage limits; a public token is not a secret, but it can still consume the account's quota.\n\n> The explicit browser `define` block in `build/vite.js` controls exactly what reaches the client: only these two keys. Everything else stays server-side.\n\n**Places and Street View never needed to be on that list** (#33): they're called from the server-side proxies in the table above, which use `GOOGLE_MAPS_SERVER_API_KEY` when it's set. Splitting it from the browser-exposed key lets each key's Google Cloud restriction actually match what it does — the browser key referrer-restricted to the APIs the client loads, the server key IP-restricted (never a referrer, since it never leaves your server) to Places + Street View Static — instead of one key that has to be either over-permissioned or broken for one of its two jobs. A single shared `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` still works if you don't split them; it just has to cover every API both sides use.\n\nNever commit real keys. `.env` is gitignored; only `.env.example` (placeholder names) is tracked. On macOS `dev-fresh.sh` can read keys from the Keychain; plain Vite uses env vars or a local `.env`, and Pinokio uses its ignored app `ENVIRONMENT` file.\n\nThe official Pinokio launcher stores optional values in its ignored local\n`pinokio/ENVIRONMENT` file and Vite explicitly denies that filename. Add,\nreplace, or remove those values through the in-app **POWER UP → Provider\nSettings** panel; the server restricts the file before writing and restarts the\nlocal app after a save. Do not submit credentials through Pinokio 8.0.40's\nnative Configure form: that release targets the wrong file for this nested\nlauncher layout and logs the submitted values. The ignored file is local\nplaintext, not encrypted storage. The macOS Keychain remains the stronger local\noption when launching through `./scripts/dev-fresh.sh`.\n\n### Configuring separate Google keys locally\n\nTerminal development uses one ignored repository-root `.env` for both\n`GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` (browser) and `GOOGLE_MAPS_SERVER_API_KEY` (server).\nThe tracked `.env.example` documents both without credentials. Vite injects\nonly the browser key; sharing an environment file does not expose the server\nkey. Provider Settings presents only the browser key as Google Maps; configure\nthe optional server key manually in the environment file. Pinokio uses\nits ignored `pinokio/ENVIRONMENT` instead, with app values and blanks taking\nprecedence over inherited global values. An absent server key retains the\nbrowser-key fallback for existing single-key setups.\n\n## Server-side proxy hardening\n\nThe data proxies under `server/providers/` are written so the browser cannot turn the server into an open relay:\n\n- **No arbitrary-URL fetching.** The CCTV frame proxy fetches only server-registered camera/frame URLs — clients cannot pass an upstream URL to fetch (SSRF mitigation). Other proxies target fixed upstream hosts.\n- **Live HLS is bounded and origin-pinned.** Registered HTTP(S) HLS sources use a Node puller that rejects redirects and off-origin playlist references, bounds playlists and segment bodies while streaming, and aborts timed-out or released sessions. At most two sessions retain 12 segments/24 MiB each, plus bounded download buffers. Stores are memory-only and idle sessions expire after 15 seconds. RTMP/ffmpeg execution is not enabled. Locally configured source URLs remain an operator trust boundary.\n- **Radio is not an audio relay.** `/api/radio/stations` contacts only allowlisted Radio Browser HTTPS hosts and paths, rejects redirects, rejects any hostname with a loopback/private/link-local/metadata/non-public A or AAAA result, and pins each TLS connection to a validated address. It returns normalized public HTTPS stream URLs; `/api/radio/click/:uuid` applies the same destination policy and accepts only station IDs from the current bounded catalog. The browser then connects directly to the broadcaster after an explicit playback action, so the broadcaster sees the listener's IP address. GEV never proxies, caches, records, or redistributes audio.\n- **No verbatim client headers upstream.** The CCTV media route is the one route that relays a request header (`Range`, for video seeking). It is parsed and canonicalized before it is forwarded: one `bytes=` range only, with every accepted form — explicit span, open-ended and suffix — bounded to the same 64 MiB ceiling the relay applies to a declared response body. Multi-range, malformed, inverted and non-`bytes` values are dropped and the request proceeds without a `Range`, as RFC 7233 §3.1 prescribes. Bounding the request bounds what is asked for: a response that declares no length — live streamed media, or a chunked body from an upstream that ignores the `Range` — has no ceiling. An upstream request the browser has stopped waiting for is cancelled rather than left running, whether the viewer leaves before the headers arrive or during the body.\n- **Transit fetches registered feeds only.** `/api/transit/vehicles/<id>` resolves the id against `src/data/transitFeeds.js`; the browser never supplies a URL, and a feed that is registered but disabled does not resolve at all. Redirects are followed manually and each hop is validated against the feed's own https origin before it is requested, so an off-origin or downgraded hop is refused rather than contacted. Bodies are capped at 8 MB, the protobuf is decoded server-side under entity-count and string-length ceilings, a differential feed is refused, and snapshots live 15 s in memory with no disk cache. A per-feed admission limiter and a failure cooldown ladder bound what this process can ask of any operator.\n- **Local receiver feeds are operator-configured and local-only.** `/api/local-receivers/aircraft` reads only the `aircraft.json` URLs in the server's `LOCAL_RECEIVER_FEEDS`; the browser never supplies an address. Each host must pass the shared tap address rule (`src/data/tapAddress.js`: loopback, RFC1918, `localhost`, `*.local`; no link-local, IPv6 or other names), the scheme must be http(s), the path must end in `aircraft.json`, and credentials, queries and fragments are refused. Invalid entries are logged at startup and never fetched. Reads use a 2 s timeout, refuse redirects, cap bodies at 2 MB and share one read per second; responses name each feed by band only and never carry upstream error text.\n- **Response-size caps and timeouts** on proxied responses.\n- **Sanitized errors** — internal error details are not echoed back to clients.\n- **Coalesced OAuth refresh** and cached successful responses only (OpenSky).\n- **Redacted debug logging.** The voice debug log (`.gev-logs/`, gitignored) strips API keys, bearer tokens, client secrets, and image data URLs before writing.\n- **Cross-site gate on cost/log endpoints.** The cost-bearing (`/api/realtime/token`, `/api/openai/hud-summary`, `/api/google/nearby-places`, `/api/google/text-search`) and log (`/api/realtime/debug-log`) endpoints refuse cross-site browser requests: a foreign or opaque `Origin`, a `Sec-Fetch-Site` other than `same-origin`/`none` (this is what blocks an `<img>`/navigation that carries no `Origin`), or any reverse-proxy/CDN forwarding header returns `403`. Non-browser loopback tools (the repo QA harnesses POST the token endpoint with no `Origin`) and the explicit `HOST=0.0.0.0` LAN opt-in keep working — the gate deliberately does not require a loopback remote address; that stricter requirement belongs only to the credential panel (`admitKeySetupRequest`). The Host check (`allowedHosts`, applied by `hostCheckPlugin` ahead of every route, since Vite's own check runs only after plugin middleware) rejects a rebinding `Host` before any handler runs, in every mode, and the gate is defense in depth behind it: the LAN opt-in keeps that check and accepts only IP addresses, `localhost` and names listed in `GEV_ALLOWED_HOSTS`. **Limit:** a name you list there is trusted like the app's own address, so list only names you control.\n- **Full Content-Security-Policy.** The dev and preview servers send a real CSP (`script-src 'self' 'unsafe-eval' blob:` plus the YouTube, Facebook and X scripts the Nepal event's embedded media loads, with a matching `frame-src` for their players and posts: no inline script and no other script origin; `blob:` covers the object URLs Cesium's bundled workers bootstrap through in the built app), alongside the existing `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and `frame-ancestors 'none'`. `'unsafe-eval'` stays because Knockout, bundled inside Cesium's widgets package, resolves the global object with `eval` at load time and the globe does not initialize without it; styles permit `'unsafe-inline'` and Google Fonts because Vite's dev client injects `<style>` elements.\n\n## Network exposure — the operator threat model\n\nThe dev server is a **key broker**: every server-side key above is spendable by anyone who can send HTTP requests to it. That shapes the defaults:\n\n- **Local-only by default.** `./scripts/dev-fresh.sh` (and the Vite config itself) bind to `localhost`, so only your machine can reach the server — and only local names are accepted (`allowedHosts` stays restricted, which also blunts DNS-rebinding tricks). Binding to all interfaces keeps that restriction: IP addresses and `localhost` work, and LAN hostnames must be listed in `GEV_ALLOWED_HOSTS` (for example `GEV_ALLOWED_HOSTS=globe.lan`); suffix and wildcard entries are ignored.\n- **LAN exposure is an explicit opt-in**: `HOST=0.0.0.0 ./scripts/dev-fresh.sh`. The launcher prints a prominent warning plus your LAN URL. Understand what opting in means: **every device on that network can drive the proxies and spend your OpenAI / Google / OpenSky / AISStream / TomTom / FIRMS quota** for as long as the server runs. Do this only on networks you trust.\n- **App-level throttles (on by default):** `GEV_RATELIMIT_OPENAI_PER_MIN` (default `30`) and `GEV_RATELIMIT_GOOGLE_PER_MIN` (default `120`) — the values the Pinokio build already ships — cap the cost-bearing endpoints per client IP per minute (over-limit requests receive a sanitized `429`). Both defaults sit well above what the app itself generates; set either to exactly `0` to run unthrottled. They are **per-IP, process-local, in-memory guards** — they reset on restart, a caller with several addresses gets a bucket per address, and they are **not billing caps**.\n- **Provider-side budgets are the real backstop.** For hard spend protection, configure limits where the money is: OpenAI platform usage limits, Google Cloud budget alerts + per-API quotas, and equivalent controls for any other keyed provider.\n- **Pinokio LAN and Cloudflare sharing are refused.** The current supported\n  Pinokio release re-reads sharing state when an app registers its Open URL and\n  logs a successful tunnel-login passcode in its own notification and terminal\n  stream. Before preflight, the launcher rewrites its app-scoped sharing controls\n  to disabled values, clears any Pinokio-global passcode from the child, and\n  pins the platform share trigger to a disabled sentinel. A stale or requested\n  sharing value is therefore discarded rather than honored, and GEV starts on\n  loopback only. Use a separately reviewed authentication proxy for remote\n  access and keep provider-side quotas as the spend backstop.\n\n## MCP server and panel\n\nGod's Eye View's tools are also served to MCP clients: over stdio (`npm run mcp`) and at `/mcp` on the development and preview servers.\n\n- **`/mcp` answers only direct local requests**: a loopback connection naming a loopback host on the port it reached, a browser `Origin` (when sent) from that same host, no proxy forwarding headers, and launcher sharing off. It accepts only JSON, so a web page cannot post to it cross-site. This is transport safety, not authentication: any program on your machine can use the tools, and some of them spend the same provider quotas as the app.\n- **What the panel's requests can reach.** In clients that display MCP Apps, the panel loads the app through the `panel_request` tool, which requests paths on the app's server. It is marked for the panel only and requires a key that each MCP server puts in its panel page, which keeps it from clients that list tools to the model without loading the panel. That key is not access control: any MCP client can read the panel page, key included, and then reach the app's files and data routes through `panel_request`, much as its other tools reach the data. Provider Settings, credential and model endpoints, `/mcp` and the development server's internal routes are refused to every caller.\n- **The panel carries the two browser keys.** The panel build (`npm run build:panel`) includes the same Google Maps key and Cesium ion token as the app, and they run inside the client's panel page, on the client's site. A key restricted by HTTP referrer must also allow that page, or the panel cannot load tiles. To keep the app's own keys narrower, build the panel with separately restricted keys in the environment of `npm run build:panel`.\n- **Embed mode is not framable by default.** `?embed=1` documents keep `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and `frame-ancestors 'none'` unless `GEV_EMBED_FRAME_ANCESTORS` names the pages that may frame them; a framing page can change what the app shows. Other documents can never be framed.\n\n## Scope & expectations\n\n- The Vite server is a **development/preview** server. If you expose it beyond localhost, put it behind your own auth/proxy and review the bindings (see the threat model above).\n- All data shown is from **public** sources. See [DATA_SOURCES.md](DATA_SOURCES.md).

[L2]   "content": "/**\n * Vite plugin: adsb.lol military aircraft proxy with 12 s response cache.\n *\n * Serves GET /api/military from https://api.adsb.lol/v2/mil. When upstream\n * fails — a thrown fetch OR a non-OK status such as 429 — the proxy serves its\n * cached body as STALE instead of relaying the failure, and it backs off from\n * upstream for the Retry-After period (bounded) so a rate limit is never\n * hammered mid-cooldown. A failure with nothing cached is relayed as-is.\n *\n * Why the non-OK case matters: the browser layer treats a relayed 429 as a\n * 45 s cooldown during which EVERY refresh (the 15 s poll and any tracking\n * resolve) reports \"adsb.lol rate limited\", which the global status chip\n * renders as LOAD FAILED while the map is still fully populated.\n *\n * @returns {import('vite').Plugin}\n */\nexport function adsbLolProxy() {\n  /** @type {string|null} Cached upstream JSON body. */\n  let _cache = null;\n  /** @type {number} Epoch-ms when the cache was populated. */\n  let _cacheAt = 0;\n  /** @type {number} Epoch-ms until which upstream is not contacted. */\n  let _cooldownUntil = 0;\n  /** @type {number} Upstream status that started the current cooldown. */\n  let _cooldownStatus = 0;\n  /** Response cache TTL (ms). */\n  const CACHE_MS = 12000;\n  /** Cooldown after a 429 when upstream sends no usable Retry-After (ms). */\n  const RATE_LIMIT_COOLDOWN_MS = 30000;\n  /** Cooldown after a 5xx (ms). */\n  const SERVER_ERROR_COOLDOWN_MS = 15000;\n  /** Bounds for an upstream-supplied Retry-After (ms). */\n  const COOLDOWN_MIN_MS = 5000;\n  const COOLDOWN_MAX_MS = 120000;\n\n  const clampCooldown = (ms) =>\n    Math.min(COOLDOWN_MAX_MS, Math.max(COOLDOWN_MIN_MS, ms));\n\n  /** Cooldown (ms) an upstream failure earns, honouring Retry-After when sane. */\n  function cooldownFor(upstream, now) {\n    const raw = upstream.headers?.get?.('retry-after');\n    if (raw) {\n      const seconds = Number(raw);\n      if (Number.isFinite(seconds) && seconds > 0)\n        return clampCooldown(seconds * 1000);\n      const at = Date.parse(raw);\n      if (Number.isFinite(at) && at > now) return clampCooldown(at - now);\n    }\n    return upstream.status === 429\n      ? RATE_LIMIT_COOLDOWN_MS\n      : SERVER_ERROR_COOLDOWN_MS;\n  }\n\n  function serve(res, status, body, cacheStatus, extra = {}) {\n    res.writeHead(status, {\n      'Content-Type': 'application/json',\n      'Cache-Control': 'no-store',\n      'X-Feed-Source': 'adsb.lol',\n      'X-Feed-Cache': cacheStatus,\n      ...(['HIT', 'STALE'].includes(cacheStatus)\n        ? {\n            'X-Feed-Age-Ms': String(Math.max(0, Date.now() - _cacheAt)),\n          }\n        : {}),\n      ...extra,\n    });\n    res.end(body);\n  }\n\n  const installMiddleware = (server) => {\n    server.middlewares.use('/api/military', async (req, res, next) => {\n      try {\n        // This mount also matches its /track route, served by its own handler.\n        if (new URL(req.url || '/', 'http://localhost').pathname !== '/')\n          return next();\n        const now = Date.now();\n        if (_cache && now - Date.now()) / 1000),\n          );\n          if (_cache) {\n            serve(res, 200, _cache, 'STALE', {\n              'X-ADS-B-Upstream-Status': String(_cooldownStatus),\n              'X-ADS-B-Retry-After-Seconds': retryAfter,\n            });\n            return;\n          }\n          serve(\n            res,\n            _cooldownStatus || 503,\n            JSON.stringify({ error: 'adsb.lol upstream cooling down' }),\n            'NONE',\n            { 'Retry-After': retryAfter },\n          );\n          return;\n        }\n        const upstream = await fetch('https://api.adsb.lol/v2/mil', {\n          headers: { 'User-Agent': 'gods-eye-view-adsblol-proxy/1.0' },\n        });\n        if (upstream.ok) {\n          const body = await upstream.text();\n          _cache = body;\n          _cacheAt = Date.now();\n          _cooldownUntil = 0;\n          _cooldownStatus = 0;\n          serve(res, 200, body, 'MISS');\n          return;\n        }\n        if (upstream.status === 429 || upstream.status >= 500) {\n          const failedAt = Date.now();\n          _cooldownUntil = failedAt + cooldownFor(upstream, failedAt);\n          _cooldownStatus = upstream.status;\n          console.warn(\n            `[adsb.lol Proxy] upstream ${upstream.status}; cooling down ${Math.round((_cooldownUntil - Date.now()) / 1000)} s${_cache ? ', serving stale' : ''}`,\n          );\n          if (_cache) {\n            // Do not wait for a failing response body before serving usable data.\n            upstream.body?.cancel().catch(() => {});\n            serve(res, 200, _cache, 'STALE', {\n              'X-ADS-B-Upstream-Status': String(upstream.status),\n              'X-ADS-B-Retry-After-Seconds': String(\n                Math.ceil((_cooldownUntil - Date.now()) / 1000),\n              ),\n            });\n            return;\n          }\n        }\n        const body = await upstream.text();\n        serve(\n          res,\n          upstream.status,\n          body,\n          'MISS',\n          _cooldownUntil > Date.now()\n            ? {\n                'Retry-After': String(\n                  Math.ceil((_cooldownUntil - Date.now()) / 1000),\n                ),\n              }\n            : {},\n        );\n      } catch (e) {\n        console.error('[adsb.lol Proxy]', e.message);\n        if (_cache) {\n          serve(res, 200, _cache, 'STALE');\n          return;\n        }\n        res.writeHead(502, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });\n        res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: 'ADS-B proxy error' }));\n      }\n    });\n  };\n  return {\n    name: 'adsblol-proxy',\n    configureServer: installMiddleware,\n    configurePreviewServer: installMiddleware,\n  };\n}",

[L93] 4. Desired end state
[L94]  GEV runs as the non-root gev service account inside a dedicated LXC; neither npm install scripts 
[L95] nor the web service run as root.
[L96]  The LXC starts automatically after acceptance. A DHCP reservation or verified existing allocation 
[L97] provides a stable address; a dynamic lease alone is reported as lease-only, not a guaranteed 
[L98] stable address.
[L99]  The Radeon Pro 570 DRM card and render node are passed into the LXC through Proxmox VE 9 
[L100] dev[n] device passthrough.
[L101]  The GPU identity, internal panel EDID/connector, active CRTC, and selected mode are recorded. 
[L102] Prefer the actual advertised 5120x2880 mode; any lower resolution is a declared degraded result.
[L103]  A dedicated Xorg server controls the selected AMD KMS device and reserved host VT; Chromium 
[L104] runs as gevdisplay on that real X display against http://127.0.0.1:4173. A small window manager 
[L105] may provide reliable kiosk/fullscreen behavior.
[L106]  The display does not sleep or blank during normal operation.
[L107]  GEV remains independently usable from another LAN browser even if the physical kiosk session is
[L108] stopped.
[L109]  No provider secret is committed to Git or baked into the browser bundle except keys explicitly 
[L110] designed to be client-visible by GEV.
[L111]  The receipt records A1-A18 individually, including command exit codes, exact versions, ownership,
[L112] network exposure, mode, renderer, sandbox evidence, changes, and rollback. A requirement is not
[L113] a test result.[L114] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 4 / 20>[L115] GMRI | GEV LXC PRD | v1.2 Audit A 4 / 20

[L147] 6. LXC creation baseline
[L148] Start with an unprivileged Debian 13 amd64 system container. Debian 12 is an available-template 
[L149] fallback only after checking its packages meet the same acceptance gates. The narrowly scoped 
[L150] privileged fallback is defined in Section 14; never change an existing rootfs UID mapping by flipping a 
[L151] config flag.
[L152] Baseline: 2 cores, cpulimit=2, 6144 MiB RAM, 2048 MiB swap allowance, 32 GiB root disk. Preserve 
[L153] at least 8 GiB of host RAM headroom after accounting for other guests; the agent may increase this 
[L154] CT to 3 cores / 8192 MiB only if measured kiosk load and host headroom justify it. Do not change host 
[L155] swap, storage layout, kernel, or other guests. Enable onboot only after the startup and identity guards 
[L156] are installed.[L157] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 5 / 20>[L158] GMRI | GEV LXC PRD | v1.2 Audit A 5 / 20

[L179] 7. GPU and DRM passthrough - Proxmox VE 9
[L180] HOST - Use Proxmox VE 9 native dev[n] passthrough for both the primary DRM node and its matching
[L181] render node. Keep amdgpu bound on the host. A render node alone cannot perform modesetting; a 
[L182] connected connector query alone does not prove display ownership. Confirm the installed pct 
[L183] help/schema before applying options. [R4, R5]
[L184] Create/query video and render groups inside the CT first. Resolve their container GIDs, select unused 
[L185] dev slots, stop only this CT, and apply the mappings. GPU_CARD and GPU_RENDER must come 
[L186] from the recorded Radeon PCI identity. These are container ownership values; do not chmod host 
[L187] devices to 0666 or give the web-service account GPU access.

[L424] 11.3 Kiosk launcher
[L425] /usr/local/bin/gev-kiosk-session (root-owned, mode 0755)
[L426] #!/bin/sh
[L427] set -eu
[L428] browser_pid=
[L429] wm_pid=
[L430] cleanup() {
[L431]  trap - EXIT
[L432]  for pid in "$browser_pid" "$wm_pid"; do
[L433]  [ -n "$pid" ] || continue
[L434]  kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || :
[L435]  done
[L436] }
[L437] trap cleanup EXIT
[L438] trap 'exit 0' INT TERM
[L439] ready() {
[L440]  timeout 5 xdpyinfo >/dev/null 2>&1 &&
[L441]  curl -fsS --connect-timeout 2 --max-time 5 \
[L442]  http://127.0.0.1:4173/ >/dev/null
[L443] }
[L444] i=0
[L445] until ready; do
[L446]  i=$((i+1))
[L447]  [ "$i" -le 60 ] || exit 1
[L448]  sleep 2
[L449] done
[L450] /etc/gev/panel-setup
[L451] xset s off
[L452] xset s noblank
[L453] xset -dpms || printf '%s\n' 'DPMS extension unavailable; verify Xorg blanking 
[L454] policy.' >&2
[L455] openbox --sm-disable &
[L456] wm_pid=$!
[L457] chromium --kiosk --no-first-run --ozone-platform=x11 \
[L458]  --user-data-dir=/home/gevdisplay/.local/share/gev/chromium \
[L459]  http://127.0.0.1:4173/ &
[L460] browser_pid=$!
[L461] failures=0
[L462] while kill -0 "$browser_pid" 2>/dev/null; do
[L463]  sleep 5
[L464]  kill -0 "$wm_pid" 2>/dev/null || exit 1
[L465]  if ready; then failures=0; else failures=$((failures+1)); fi
[L466]  [ "$failures" -lt 3 ] || exit 1
[L467] done
[L468] # A closed browser is restarted by the kiosk unit.
[L469] exit 1
[L470] Readiness uses an authenticated X request plus the local HTTP service, not socket existence. The 
[L471] supervisor restarts the browser after sustained app/X failure or browser exit; it only terminates its own 
[L472] children. A provider outage must not be used as this liveness signal. Run bash/sh syntax checks 
[L473] before installation.

[L557] 12. Network and exposure rules
[L558] 100.98.1.114 is the supplied Proxmox management endpoint, not a CT address, LAN prefix, gateway, 
[L559] or proof that a particular VPN product is installed. Preserve the existing SSH/overlay route and trust 
[L560] configuration. Discover the actual bridge and authorized client network; do not grant all of 
[L561] 100.64.0.0/10 access. [R10]
[L562] Before changing HOST from loopback to 0.0.0.0, enforce persistent CT-scoped ingress filtering: 
[L563] loopback and established replies allowed; TCP/4173 allowed only from the resolved trusted clients; 
[L564] required DHCP/ICMP traffic allowed; other unsolicited ingress denied. Apply equivalent IPv6 
[L565] restrictions or keep the service unbound from IPv6 and verify listeners. Use the existing effective PVE 
[L566] CT firewall when available; otherwise configure the new CT's own firewall. Never enable/flush a host￾wide ruleset or change management-network policy for this job.
[L567] Verify the effective rules, not just a firewall checkbox. Test allowed access, an untrusted source where 
[L568] available, and persistence through CT restart. An unperformed negative network test is NOT RUN. If 
[L569] trust or filtering cannot be established, leave GEV on loopback, preserve the kiosk, and report network
[L570] acceptance as blocked rather than opening the service broadly.
[L571] Do not configure public port forwards, tunnels, or an unreviewed reverse proxy. The inspected GEV 
[L572] source rejects forwarding headers on cost/log and local administrative routes; a generic proxy can 
[L573] break or alter those protections. Preserve Host/Origin checks and loopback-only Provider Settings and
[L574] /mcp. Keep default rate limits nonzero; they are not hard billing limits. Use only credentials already 
[L575] authorized for this deployment. [R3]
[L576] Record the real CT URL and the existing route used to reach it. If no existing overlay/subnet route 
[L577] reaches the CT, do not claim that browsing 100.98.1.114:4173 will work. Keyless operation still 
[L578] requires external network access for live feeds and tiles. Remote microphone access requires a 
[L579] browser-secure context; plain HTTP on a LAN IP does not establish voice readiness. Missing voice 
[L580] keys/audio/HTTPS are separately reported optional capability states, not silently counted as working
