[L669] 14. Failure handling and permitted fallbacks
[L670] Start unprivileged and diagnose exact failures after correct device/GID/VT configuration. If required 
[L671] KMS/VT operations remain incompatible with the unprivileged namespace, the documented dedicated 
[L672] privileged-LXC fallback remains authorized: save a verified backup and manifest, then restore/recreate
[L673] into a separate free CTID with appropriate ID mapping. Never toggle unprivileged on an existing rootfs,
[L674] overwrite another guest, or delete the only recoverable copy.
[L675] A graphics privilege failure is not permission to run the web app/browser as root. Preserve 
[L676] AppArmor/seccomp, the browser sandbox, and a minimal device list. Do not use an empty capability￾drop list, unconfined profile, all-device allow rule, host PID/network sharing, or VFIO as a shortcut. 
[L677] Record any narrowly justified CT capability/profile change and its exact denial evidence.
[L678] If no usable internal-panel connector is exposed, retain the inventory and stop display mutation. A 
[L679] lower stable advertised mode may keep the console useful, but must be reported as DEGRADED￾MODE. Never force an unadvertised timing. If the GPU is already owned by an unrelated active 
[L680] workload, do not evict it.
[L681] A healthy LAN service must survive display troubleshooting. Before a privileged candidate takes over, 
[L682] preserve the old service and test the candidate independently; never attach two competing Xorg 
[L683] masters to the same panel or use two guests with the same IP.[L684] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 16 / 20>[L685] GMRI | GEV LXC PRD | v1.2 Audit A 16 / 20
[L686] If tests on the frozen current-main candidate fail, record them, preserve the prior known-good release 
[L687] and troubleshoot only deployment causes. Do not change application semantics or delete tests to 
[L688] make the run pass. Distinguish an upstream feed outage from an application failure and respect rate￾limit backoff.
[L689] Use at most three attempts per identified recoverable cause, with evidence of what changed; do not 
[L690] repeat destructive guesses. On a hard blocker, preserve working services, reverse only this run's 
[L691] unsafe changes, retain the candidate/logs, and return a precise PARTIAL/BLOCKED receipt without 
[L692] waiting for routine input.
[L693] 15. Update and rollback discipline
[L694] Stage updates in a new /opt/gev/releases directory; never run npm ci, git reset, or an in-place pull in 
[L695] the active release while GEV is serving it. Snapshot the current unit files, .env, Node target, 
[L696] profile/state and active symlink before any switch. Preserve old artifacts until the new deployment 
[L697] passes acceptance. [R3]
[L698] Run candidate doctor/tests/build as gev. Start its real provider server on an unused loopback-only 
[L699] staging port with strictPort and validate UI and API behavior. Do not expose that port or use a second 
[L700] physical Xorg server. A failed candidate must not disturb the running release.
[L701] For promotion, stop gev-xorg.service (which stops the kiosk), then stop gev.service. Replace the root￾owned active symlink by a same-filesystem atomic rename; change the recorded Node symlink only if 
[L702] part of the tested candidate. Start GEV, then Xorg/kiosk, and run acceptance. Keep the service outage
[L703] bounded and measured.
[L704] On failure, stop the candidate services and restore the prior symlink, Node target, matching 
[L705] configuration and any required state backup; then restart and verify. Do not reinstall dependencies 
[L706] from the network as the primary rollback path. Record the failed SHA/configuration and update the 
[L707] known-good manifest only after successful acceptance.
[L708] During the first installation, there may be no earlier application version. Establish and back up the 
[L709] initial working release, then test rejection/restoration using an isolated intentionally failing deployment 
[L710] configuration. Label this as baseline rollback mechanics, not a proven cross-version application-data 
[L711] migration.

[L740] 17. Local-agent execution directive
[L741] Directive | Execute this audit revision end-to-end against 100.98.1.114 using existing authorized 
[L742] access. Resolve routine choices from live state. Deploy the GMRI fork to an LXC, use native dev[n] 
[L743] GPU/DRM access, and deliver both trusted-network GEV and the physical-panel kiosk. Run A1-A18,
[L744] preserve rollback/evidence, and return the receipt. Do not wait for routine decisions; do not describe 
[L745] a partial result as complete.
[L746] 17.1 Connection and authority policy
[L747] AGENT - Connect to 100.98.1.114 over the already-authorized management route, using existing SSH
[L748] credentials/agent material and host-key trust. Use an existing approved sudo-capable account when 
[L749] root login is not permitted. Record the resolved hostname/identity. Do not change authentication, 
[L750] replace a host key on blind trust, or re-enroll the host into a different overlay.
[L751] ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes root@100.98.1.114
[L752] Authentication failure is not the only possible blocker. Unreachable management, untrusted host 
[L753] identity, degraded storage, insufficient resources, a conflicting live GPU owner or an unsafe security 
[L754] change also require a precise BLOCKED/PARTIAL result. Retry transient connectivity safely, use only 
[L755] existing authorized credentials/routes, and never brute-force, reset credentials or disable host-key 
[L756] checking to continue.
[L757] 17.2 Autonomous decision policy
[L758] The agent owns routine deployment choices. Resolve them from live state using the following order of 
[L759] preference:
[L760] 1. Preserve existing host services and running containers/VMs. Never modify or delete an unrelated 
[L761] guest to make room.
[L762] 2. Separate template storage from CT rootfs storage. Prefer healthy existing storage with suitable 
[L763] content types, free capacity for the guest plus rollback, and no disruptive migration or pool creation.
[L764] 3. Discover the real trusted application/LAN bridge and VLAN. Do not bridge an overlay/TUN interface,
[L765] infer a subnet from 100.98.1.114, or modify the host default route.
[L766] 4. Reuse only a CT identified by this deployment's manifest. Otherwise obtain a cluster-wide unused 
[L767] CTID and recheck before creation; never reuse an unrelated guest ID.
[L768] 5. Prefer an available official Debian 13 amd64 template. If only Debian 12 is available, verify 
[L769] package/runtime compatibility and record the fallback. No template approval prompt is needed.
[L770] 6. Use DHCP unless an existing authorized static allocation/reservation is available. Record the lease; 
[L771] claim a stable address only when the reservation/allocation is verified. Do not modify the router or infer
[L772] availability from a failed ping.[L773] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 18 / 20>[L774] GMRI | GEV LXC PRD | v1.2 Audit A 18 / 20
[L775] 7. Deploy keyless unless an approved secret source explicitly authorizes credentials for this 
[L776] deployment. Missing optional keys do not block the baseline; neither do they establish paid-provider or
[L777] voice acceptance.
[L778] 8. Resolve the Radeon by PCI identity, then card/render nodes, internal panel EDID/output and one 
[L779] unused host VT. Validate ownership and scanout separately. Keep boot-time remapping scoped to this
[L780] CT.
[L781] 9. Start unprivileged; use only the Section 14 documented dedicated privileged fallback if the actual 
[L782] KMS/VT operation cannot be satisfied. Preserve recovery artifacts, the application UID and Chromium 
[L783] sandbox.
[L784] 10. Preserve all unrelated guests/services, management access and recovery console. Prefer 
[L785] reversible changes with local rollback files. Do not treat unattended execution as permission to 
[L786] broaden the assignment.
[L787] 17.3 End-to-end execution sequence
[L788] Execute continuously in this order without waiting for operator confirmation between successful 
[L789] stages:
[L790] Phase 1 - Connect and inventory: authenticate from AGENT to 100.98.1.114, verify identity, create a 
[L791] run ID, and retain HOST hardware, storage, network, guest, driver, GPU-owner and firewall 
[L792] observations. Confirm existing recovery access.
[L793] Phase 2 - Allocate: resolve free CTID, template/root storage, resources, real bridge/VLAN and address
[L794] method. Write validated run parameters to the manifest; do not invent missing values.
[L795] Phase 3 - Create the CT: create the unprivileged guest with onboot initially disabled. Verify DNS, 
[L796] package access and routes. Create service/display groups and accounts; establish CT-scoped 
[L797] network protection before non-loopback app binding.
[L798] Phase 4 - Map graphics: stop this CT, set native dev[n] mappings with actual CT GIDs, reserve/map 
[L799] only the required physical VT devices, then restart. Install the GPU identity resolver/guard and 
[L800] preserve original host VT/getty state.
[L801] Phase 5 - Stage GEV: verify/install the exact Node runtime, resolve origin/main once, clone/stage that 
[L802] SHA as gev, configure provenance, install all locked dependencies and run actual repository gates. 
[L803] Retain the logs.
[L804] Phase 6 - Start the application: promote the tested release, install the non-root gev.service, verify GEV
[L805] and provider middleware on loopback, then enable trusted-network binding only behind verified rules. 
[L806] Record the real CT URL and route.
[L807] Phase 7 - Start the physical kiosk: install CT graphics packages, bind Xorg to the Radeon and 
[L808] reserved VT, generate per-start Xauthority, correlate the internal output, install panel-setup and the 
[L809] non-root supervised Chromium session. Prove scanout, hardware rendering and sandbox state.
[L810] Phase 8 - Persistence and rollback: validate all units/helpers; enable CT onboot and the targeted GPU
[L811] preparation ordering. Run two CT restart cycles, component-failure tests and retained-artifact rollback. 
[L812] A host reboot is allowed only if unrelated workloads will not be interrupted AND tested recovery access
[L813] and reconnect automation are available. Otherwise defer A1 without asking the operator or changing 
[L814] other systems.
[L815] Phase 9 - Acceptance: execute A1-A18 and the 15-minute load observation. Capture actual output, 
[L816] ownership, renderer, sandbox, network/negative checks, provider status and electronic panel 
[L817] evidence. Do not promote missing evidence into PASS.[L818] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 19 / 20>[L819] GMRI | GEV LXC PRD | v1.2 Audit A 19 / 20
[L820] Phase 10 - Return the result: retain exact manifests/logs/backups on the HOST, copy the deployment 
[L821] receipt to the CT and AGENT workspace, and report DEPLOYED, DEPLOYED / HOST-REBOOT￾DEFERRED, DEGRADED-MODE, PARTIAL or BLOCKED as justified. Include the verified URL and 
[L822] recovery commands.
[L823] 17.4 Non-interruption / fallback rules
[L824] Do not ask the operator to choose storage, CTID, bridge, DHCP versus static, Debian version, 
[L825] resource sizing, connector name, browser package, service naming, or whether to proceed keyless. 
[L826] Discover and decide.
[L827] Do not stop for optional provider keys, a missing paid basemap, or routine environment choices. The 
[L828] required baseline is keyless GEV plus the real GPU-driven internal-panel kiosk and trusted-network 
[L829] access. Keyless is not network-independent; provider outages must remain visible rather than 
[L830] replaced with simulated live data.
[L831] Retry only with a diagnosed reversible correction and a bounded attempt count. Capture evidence 
[L832] before modifying a failing path. Keep the LAN app available during display work; keep the panel 
[L833] available during optional-provider troubleshooting.
[L834] If the candidate deployment cannot satisfy a hard acceptance gate, leave the host in the safest known￾good state, retain logs and the failed container rather than deleting evidence unless deletion is 
[L835] necessary for a clean rollback, and explain the blocker in the deployment receipt.
[L836] No unrelated host upgrade, kernel replacement, Proxmox repository change, storage migration, 
[L837] firewall redesign, or network-wide change is authorized by this PRD.
[L838] 17.5 Completion definition
[L839] Completion requires the Section 13 mandatory gates, both requested surfaces, persistent non-root 
[L840] application/browser processes, native GPU/DRM access, and durable receipts. The stated A1 deferral 
[L841] and native-mode degradation have distinct result labels. A plan, HTTP-only service, headless render, 
[L842] optional fallback suggestion, or request for routine choices is not the completed assignment.
